comparison: Both evaluate DyNoPy's methodological framework and novelty (C5-C7, C22-C24, C52, C163-C165, C179-C184). OpenEval focuses on technical consistency and documentation; peer reviewers emphasize the unified framework's novelty and utility, with explicit affirmation that 'no unified framework exists' prior to this work.

Both address DyNoPy's advantages and novelty (C163-C165, C179-C181). OpenEval validates advantages through demonstrated results; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the method 'convincingly demonstrate[s]' utility and provides 'biologically relevant insights.' Strong agreement on method's contribution.

Both address β-lactamase background (C25-C51 vs C28-C51, C8). OpenEval validates extensive citations establishing biological context; peer reviewers accept test system choice and clinical relevance without criticism. Agreement on appropriateness of background and test systems.

Both evaluate CV selection methodology and its impact on coupling detection (C54-C61, C166-C167, C228-C229). OpenEval provides detailed validation with quantitative data; peer reviewers implicitly accept CV approach as part of validated methodology without challenge.

Both address the superiority of combining coevolution with dynamics (C62-C66). OpenEval validates with specific data from Supplementary file 1c and Figure 3; peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating the method 'convincingly demonstrate[s] that integrating signals...substantially overcomes...either method in isolation.'

Both evaluate community detection and recovery of known functional sites (C67-C70 overlap). OpenEval validates eight communities with detailed structural analysis; peer reviewers affirm method's ability to 'show clinically relevance of mutations,' supporting validation capability.

Both address L162 predictions and mechanistic insights (C75-C83, C71-C74, C170-C174). OpenEval validates extensive coupling network with literature support; peer reviewers explicitly affirm predictive capability, stating method 'could...predict new potential evolutionary mutations.' Strong agreement on predictive value.

Both evaluate L162 and N136 predictions with mechanistic explanations (C72, C74, C170-C174). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate speculation; peer reviewers affirm predictive capability and mechanistic insights, validating explanations for absence of these mutations in SHV-1.

Both evaluate N136 mechanistic findings (C84-C96). OpenEval validates coupling patterns with extensive citations; peer reviewers accept detailed mechanistic findings without challenge, implicitly validating through overall positive assessment of method's utility.

Both address hydrophobic cavity and stability networks (C100-C104 overlap). OpenEval validates recovery of known structural features; peer reviewers accept findings, noting method reveals 'interaction patterns that are larger than simple couples,' supporting complex network identification.

Both evaluate stability-related couplings and hydrophobic networks (C105-C112). OpenEval validates with citations to established understanding; peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, consistent with method's validated ability to reveal complex stability networks.

Both address distant mutation coupling and epistatic relationships (C117-C126). OpenEval validates mechanistic explanations with citations; peer reviewers affirm method provides 'biologically relevant insights' and predictive power for understanding distant mutations.

Both evaluate co-occurring mutations R205 and G238 (C127-C138). OpenEval validates with extensive citations and mechanistic explanation; peer reviewers accept findings, consistent with method's ability to reveal 'community analysis...interaction patterns that are larger than simple couples.'

Both address PDC-3 Ω-loop findings and R2-loop differential effects (C143-C152, C146-C152 overlap). OpenEval validates method's explanatory power for previously unexplained observations; peer reviewers accept findings as providing 'biologically relevant insights.'

Both evaluate PDC-3 community detection and known site recovery (C143-C145). OpenEval validates identification of all known Ω-loop mutations; peer reviewers affirm method's validation and prediction capabilities for PDC-3.

Both evaluate G204 predictions for PDC-3 (C153-C162). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature requiring experimental confirmation; peer reviewers SUPPORT predictions, stating method 'could...predict new potential evolutionary mutations,' showing more confidence in speculative predictions.

Both address DyNoPy's validation and predictive capabilities (C175-C178). OpenEval validates with appropriate acknowledgment of speculation; peer reviewers explicitly affirm both capabilities, stating method 'could not only show clinically relevance...but also predict new potential evolutionary mutations.'

Both evaluate MD simulation methodology (C210-C224). OpenEval validates detailed methodology with appropriate citations for reproducibility; peer reviewers accept without challenge, with editor stating 'the data are solid,' implicitly validating simulation approach.

Both address computational methodology for coevolution analysis (C190-C196 overlap). OpenEval validates with specific tools, databases, and parameters; peer reviewers accept methodology without challenge, with positive assessment implicitly validating technical implementation.

Both evaluate DyNoPy methodology and graph construction (C198-C206). OpenEval validates internal consistency and documentation; peer reviewers affirm method 'convincingly demonstrate[s]' utility, validating overall methodological framework.

Both address gaps in existing methods (C3, C18, C21, C1-C21). OpenEval validates gap identification through literature review; peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'no unified framework exists' prior to this work, strongly supporting the identified gap and motivation.

Both address β-lactamase background and clinical relevance (C25-C27). OpenEval validates extensive background citations; peer reviewers accept as established factual background, acknowledging clinical relevance for drug discovery applications.

Both evaluate future applications to multi-functional proteins (C168-C169). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of empirical support; peer reviewers SUPPORT broader applicability, noting 'implications in...drug discovery...and protein design,' showing more confidence in speculative extensions.

Partial overlap on CV selection and method superiority (C60-C61 in both, but peer R4 focuses on C62-C66). OpenEval validates CV filtering efficiency; peer reviewers emphasize superiority of combined approach over isolated methods.

Minimal overlap (C71, C73). OpenEval addresses community detection validation; peer reviewers focus on L162 predictive capability. Both support method's ability to identify functionally important sites.
